title: core runs git in English, so its error text can be read on any machine
description:
Three places in core read git's stderr as English: packages/core/src/sync.ts:596 (`fetchBoard`, `/couldn't find remote ref/`), packages/core/src/sync.ts:624 (the push-rejected regex `non-fast-forward|fetch first|rejected|...`) and packages/core/src/digest.ts:111 (the same missing-ref check). On a machine whose locale is not English — this Mac speaks Turkish, git says `onulmaz: refs/heads/sober/board uzak başvurusu bulunamadı` — none of them match. `fetchBoard` then reads the ordinary first sync as an unreachable remote and refuses with 'origin could not be reached', and `pnpm integration` is red on 137 tests (every sync path: board, conflict, wire, cli, sync, team, digest, distribute, client, dashboard, three in mcp). CI is green only because the runners are English.

Every git call in core goes through one `exec` in packages/core/src/git.ts (line ~44; `git`, `gitWithEnv`, `gitVerbatim` all land there). Fix it once, there: spawn git with `LC_ALL: 'C'` placed after `...process.env` and before the caller's `...env`, so the user's locale never reaches git and a caller can still override. That pins every message the three regexes read; the regexes themselves do not change. Add one test in packages/core/src/git.test.ts (or next to the existing git tests) that sets `LANG`/`LC_ALL` to a non-English locale in `process.env` for the call, runs a fetch of a missing ref on a local bare remote, and asserts the error text contains `couldn't find remote ref` — the assertion that fails today on a Turkish machine. Do not touch the sync or digest regexes and do not add a per-call env at any call site: the point is that no future git call can forget it.
